content: When co-administering CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl, it is essential to monitor patients closely for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals. Adjustments to the fentanyl dosage should be considered until stable drug effects are achieved. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (both transdermal and transmucosal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose accordingly. Atazanavir decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Conversely, fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects, such as Cushing-like symptoms. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Interrupt and reduce the gilteritinib dosage in cases of serious or life-threatening toxicity. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors, or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 and OATP1B1 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Clinical trials have shown an increased risk of ALT elevations when atazanavir is co-administered with glecaprevir. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations. For treatment-naïve patients, take atazanavir simultaneously with the H2-receptor antagonist (H2RA) or at least 10 hours afterward. Refer to dosage adjustment recommendations for treatment-experienced patients. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow dosage modification recommendations if adverse reactions occur. Idelalisib also increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir and indinavir exhibit pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially leading to additive hyperbilirubinemia. Concomitant use is not recommended. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan (including liposomal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and UGT1A1. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations. Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) doses should not exceed a dose comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken ~12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib, lefamulin, lemborexant, lenacapavir, and leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Atazanavir may alter estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with oral contraceptives containing levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use a nonhormonal contraceptive method. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor, increase the lorlatinib dose to the previous level after three plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Discontinue antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period for elimination. ARTs may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin, macitentan, and mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives, increase the lurbinectedin dose to the pre-co-administration level. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of midazolam (including intranasal formulations) and methylergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of midostaurin, modafinil, nefazodone, neratinib, and nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with nevirapine is contraindicated. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of niragestat, nizatidine, and omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations. PPI doses should not exceed a dose comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken ~12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of osimertinib, oxycodone, palbociclib, palovarotene, and pantoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of pazopanib, pemigatinib, pexidartinib, pimavanserin, pirtobrutinib, and pomalidomide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the doses of these drugs as per their respective prescribing information. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ponatinib, pralsetinib, quetiapine, and rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the quetiapine dose to 1/6th of the current dose and monitor for adverse reactions. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ranolazine, red yeast rice, repotrectinib, resmetirom, and ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with ranolazine is contraindicated. For ribociclib, reduce the starting dose to 400 mg/day if co-administration is unavoidable. Rifampin and rifapentine decrease the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant, romidepsin, rosuvastatin, and ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the ruxolitinib starting dose to 10 mg BID with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib, selumetinib, silodosin, siponimod, and sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with silodosin and sirolimus is contraindicated. For selpercatinib, reduce the dose as per prescribing information. Sodium bicarbonate and sodium citrate/citric acid decrease the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sparsentan, St. John’s Wort, stiripentol, suvorexant, tadalafil, tamoxifen, and tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with St. John’s Wort is contraindicated. For tadalafil, stop administration >24 hours before initiating protease inhibitors (PIs), restart 7 days after PI initiation at 20 mg once daily, and increase to 40 mg once daily based on tolerability.
